translations.complex_sample.logistic_guide.estimates: Main tables report OR and 95% CI. Coefficient appendices report B, design-based SE, Wald F and p. The shared denominator degrees of freedom appear in the notes. Z is not repeated. User labels are retained.
translations.complex_sample.logistic_guide.flow: Case counts start from the data supplied to this analysis after case selection or splitting. Sequential exclusions are counted once. Outcome-only, predictor-only and joint missingness are mutually exclusive; variable-specific missing counts may overlap. Complete-case analysis does not establish random missingness.
translations.complex_sample.logistic_guide.odds: Multinomial OR compares an outcome category with the reference category. Ordinal OR compares higher versus lower cumulative categories and assumes equal slopes across thresholds. A non-significant proportional-odds diagnostic does not prove that assumption.
translations.complex_sample.logistic_guide.screening: Weighted GVIF describes predictor geometry, not inflation of the fitted survey-sandwich variance. Cells below five are screening flags, not a validity threshold. These checks do not rule out separation, misspecification or proportional-odds violations.
translations.complex_sample.logistic_guide.stability: Optimizer codes and IRLS iteration counts provide different evidence. No warnings or numerical flags does not establish model validity. Coefficient magnitudes depend on units and coding; probability-boundary checks are not formal separation tests.
translations.complex_sample.logistic_guide.scope: The non-proportional-odds candidate has been implemented as an example script, not a general analysis-menu option. Study aims, weights and covariate rationale still determine the final model. Select All in Word/HWPX export to include explanations and diagnostic appendices.

translations.sample_size.result.paired_formula: Cohen's dz = mean paired difference / SD of paired differences.
translations.sample_size.result.one_sample_formula: Cohen's d = (sample mean - null mean) / SD.
translations.sample_size.result.independent_formula: Cohen's d = (M1 - M2) / pooled SD; Hedges' g = J x d with J = 1 - 3 / (4df - 1).
translations.sample_size.result.group_n_error: Both group sample sizes must be at least 2.
translations.sample_size.result.groups_error: Number of groups must be at least 2.
translations.sample_size.result.total_n_error: Total sample size must be greater than the number of groups.
translations.sample_size.result.odds_ratio: Odds ratio = [p1 / (1 - p1)] / [p2 / (1 - p2)]; 2x2 tables with a zero cell use a 0.5 continuity correction.
translations.sample_size.result.point_biserial: Point-biserial r is Pearson r for a binary and continuous variable; for a two-group contrast, d = 2r / sqrt(1 - r^2).
translations.sample_size.result.correlation_f: For a one-degree-of-freedom effect, r = sqrt(F / (F + df_error)).
translations.sample_size.result.correlation_r2: r = sqrt(R-squared); the sign is not identifiable from R-squared alone.
translations.sample_size.result.anova_eta: For one-way ANOVA, df_effect = groups - 1 and df_error = total N - groups; partial eta squared = F * df_effect / (F * df_effect + df_error); omega squared is also reported; Cohen's f = sqrt(partial eta-squared / [1 - partial eta-squared]).
translations.sample_size.result.anova_omega: For one-way ANOVA, df_effect = groups - 1 and df_error = total N - groups; partial omega squared is approximated as (F * df_effect - df_effect) / (F * df_effect + df_error + 1), bounded at 0.
translations.sample_size.result.anova_f: Cohen's f = sqrt(eta-squared / [1 - eta-squared]); the same conversion is used for partial eta-squared.
translations.sample_size.result.ancova_adjusted: ANCOVA adjusted f = unadjusted f / sqrt(1 - covariate R-squared).
translations.sample_size.result.manova_pillai: For MANOVA planning, f2 = Pillai's V / (1 - Pillai's V), and f = sqrt(f2).
translations.sample_size.result.manova_wilks: For MANOVA planning, Wilks' lambda is converted using s = min(number of dependent variables, groups - 1): eta2 = 1 - lambda^(1/s), f2 = eta2 / (1 - eta2), and f = sqrt(f2).
translations.sample_size.result.ancova_eta: For one-way ANCOVA/group contrast planning, df_effect = groups - 1 and df_error = total N - groups; partial eta squared = F * df_effect / (F * df_effect + df_error); Cohen's f = sqrt(partial eta-squared / [1 - partial eta-squared]).
translations.sample_size.result.rank_biserial: Rank-biserial r = 2U / (n1 n2) - 1; this is equivalent to Cliff's delta orientation.
translations.sample_size.result.epsilon: Epsilon squared = (H - k + 1) / (N - k), bounded at 0.
translations.sample_size.result.matched_counts: Matched-pair odds ratio = b / c for discordant pairs; if either discordant cell is zero, a 0.5 continuity correction is used.
translations.sample_size.result.matched_g: Cohen's g = p01 / (p01 + p10) - 0.5 for the discordant-pair direction.
translations.sample_size.result.matched_probs: Matched-pair odds ratio = p01 / p10; log odds ratio = log(p01 / p10).
translations.sample_size.result.logistic_d: log odds ratio = log(OR); approximate Cohen's d = log(OR) * sqrt(3) / pi.
translations.sample_size.result.interaction_f2: Interaction Cohen's f2 = delta R-squared / (1 - delta R-squared).
translations.sample_size.result.gee_binary: Cohen's h = 2 asin(sqrt(p1)) - 2 asin(sqrt(p2)); planning effect = h / sqrt(design effect).
translations.sample_size.result.gee_change: Cohen's d = [(post - pre) group 1 - (post - pre) group 2] / common outcome SD.
translations.sample_size.result.gee_parameter: Cohen's d = GEE group x time parameter estimate B / common outcome SD.
translations.sample_size.result.gee_means: Cohen's d = (estimated mean group 1 - estimated mean group 2) / common outcome SD.
translations.sample_size.result.glmm_binary: Binary logit GLMM: log(OR) = B, OR = exp(B), approximate latent-scale d = log(OR) * sqrt(3) / pi. For probabilities, odds ratio and Cohen's h are both reported.
translations.sample_size.result.glmm_count: Count GLMM with log link: log(IRR) = B, IRR = exp(B). For rates, rate ratio = rate1 / rate2.
translations.sample_size.result.glmm_gaussian: Gaussian identity-link mixed model: Cohen's d = fixed-effect coefficient B / residual SD.
translations.sample_size.result.lmm_spss: Omnibus partial eta squared = F * df_effect / (F * df_effect + df_error). Optional pairwise Cohen's dz = mean difference / sqrt(Var_i + Var_j - 2Cov_ij).
translations.sample_size.result.lmm_glimmpse: Standardized change effect = last-minus-first mean contrast / residual SD; planning effect = d * sqrt(m / design effect).
translations.sample_size.result.lmm_simple: Repeated-measures planning effect = standardized fixed effect * sqrt(m / [1 + (m - 1)ICC]).
translations.analysis.ui.normal_residuals_are_not_exp: Normal residuals are not expected for GLM-family link-scale models.
translations.analysis.ui.assess_whether_the_selected_: Assess whether the selected outcome family and link match the data instead of relying on normal residuals.
translations.analysis.ui.at_least_3_residuals_are_req: At least 3 residuals are required for Shapiro-Wilk screening.
translations.analysis.ui.use_graphical_residual_revie: Use graphical residual review when more observations are available.
translations.analysis.ui.the_normality_screening_test: The normality screening test could not be computed.
translations.analysis.ui.review_q_q_plots_or_use_boot: Review Q-Q plots or use bootstrap / robust inference if residual normality is doubtful.
translations.analysis.ui.use_robust_or_bootstrap_conf: Use robust or bootstrap confidence intervals; for clearly non-Gaussian outcomes, switch to GEE / GLMM with the appropriate family.
translations.analysis.ui.continue_with_the_selected_g: Continue with the selected Gaussian model; still review residual plots for shape and outliers.
translations.sample_size.result.survival_hr: Log hazard ratio = log(HR). For survival meta-analysis, use log(HR) with its standard error.
translations.sample_size.result.equivalence_distance: Equivalence distance = margin - abs(observed effect); standardized distance divides this value by SD or pooled Bernoulli SD.
translations.sample_size.result.noninferiority_distan: Non-inferiority distance = margin + observed effect for a -margin boundary; standardized distance divides this value by SD or pooled Bernoulli SD.
translations.sample_size.result.diagnostic_auc: AUC is reported directly; AUC difference = AUC - null AUC; approximate Cohen's d = sqrt(2) * qnorm(AUC).
translations.sample_size.result.gamma_ratio: For gamma regression with a log link, mean ratio = exp(beta), and log mean ratio = beta.
translations.sample_size.result.count_ratio: For Poisson and negative binomial regression with a log link, incidence rate ratio = exp(beta), and log incidence rate ratio = beta.
translations.sample_size.result.cluster_binary: Cohen's h is adjusted for cluster planning as h / sqrt(1 + (m - 1)ICC).
translations.sample_size.result.cluster_stepped: Planning effect applies d / sqrt([1 + (m - 1)ICC] * periods / [periods - 1]).
translations.sample_size.result.cluster_continuous: Continuous cluster planning effect = d / sqrt(1 + (m - 1)ICC).
translations.sample_size.result.precision_mean: Standardized half-width = desired mean CI half-width / SD.
translations.sample_size.result.precision_proportion: Bernoulli-standardized half-width = desired proportion CI half-width / sqrt(p[1 - p]).
translations.sample_size.result.precision_correlation: Correlation precision uses Fisher's z transformation; z half-width is computed from r +/- desired raw-r half-width.
translations.sample_size.result.reliability_alpha: Alpha difference = alpha - reference alpha; Bonett-style transformed alpha uses log(1 - alpha).
translations.sample_size.result.reliability_icc: ICC difference = ICC - reference ICC; transformed ICC uses Fisher's z.
translations.sample_size.result.reliability_kappa: Cohen's kappa is reported directly; observed agreement assumes equal category prevalence.
translations.sample_size.result.reliability_agreement: Bland-Altman limits of agreement are mean difference +/- 1.96 * SD of paired differences.
translations.sample_size.result.sem_rmsea: RMSEA effect is alternative RMSEA - null RMSEA; noncentrality difference per N = df * (RMSEA_alt^2 - RMSEA_null^2).
translations.sample_size.result.sem_parameter: Standardized SEM parameter effect is the expected standardized coefficient; Fisher's z = atanh(parameter).
translations.sample_size.result.sem_complexity: Complexity effect summarizes observed/latent/path burden per free parameter plus Fisher-z transformed expected loading and path effects.
translations.analysis.ui.no_overdispersion_adjustment: No overdispersion adjustment is suggested by this screening rule.
translations.analysis.ui.consider_robust_sandwich_inf: Consider robust sandwich inference, alternative family, or subject-level random effects depending on the selected model.
translations.analysis.ui.for_gee_glmm_rely_on_robust_: For GEE / GLMM, rely on robust sandwich inference and check model family fit.
translations.analysis.ui.use_cluster_robust_standard_: Use cluster-robust standard errors if heteroskedasticity is plausible.
translations.analysis.ui.conventional_variance_assump: Conventional variance assumptions look acceptable by this screening test.
translations.analysis.ui.use_heteroskedasticity_robus: Use heteroskedasticity-robust or subject-clustered standard errors.
translations.analysis.ui.review_the_random_effects_di: Review the random-effects distribution graphically when enough clusters are available.
translations.analysis.ui.use_graphical_review_and_sen: Use graphical review and sensitivity analysis; consider GEE if population-averaged inference is the primary target.
translations.analysis.ui.residual_degrees_of_freedom_: Residual degrees of freedom were not available for overdispersion screening.
translations.analysis.ui.for_count_or_binary_clustere: For count or binary clustered outcomes, review dispersion and sparse cells before final interpretation.
translations.analysis.ui.breusch_pagan_screening_is_m: Breusch-Pagan screening is mainly intended for Gaussian mean models.
translations.analysis.ui.breusch_pagan_screening_coul: Breusch-Pagan screening could not be computed for this model frame.
translations.analysis.ui.install_lmtest_or_use_residu: Install lmtest or use residual-vs-fitted plots.
translations.analysis.ui.review_random_effect_quantil: Review random-effect quantile plots if random-effect distribution is important.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_t: Uses the noncentral t distribution for exact t-test power when available; unequal two-group allocation uses a normal approximation with Cohen's d.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_rank_omnibus: Uses a large-sample noncentral chi-square approximation for rank-based omnibus tests.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_rank_pair: Approximates Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney sample size from the corresponding t-test effect size using asymptotic relative efficiency.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_proportion: Uses normal-approximation power for one- or two-proportion tests with optional allocation ratio.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_chisquare: Uses Cohen's w with the noncentral chi-square distribution.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_correlation: Uses Fisher's z transformation for Pearson correlation power and sample size.
translations.analysis.ui.if_repeated_measures_are_den: If repeated measures are dense, consider GEE correlation structures or cluster-robust inference.
translations.analysis.ui.no_additional_serial_correla: No additional serial-correlation adjustment is suggested by this test.
translations.analysis.ui.if_common_shocks_are_likely_: If common shocks are likely, include time fixed effects or use panel-robust inference.
translations.analysis.ui.use_time_fixed_effects_when_: Use time fixed effects when common period shocks are plausible.
translations.analysis.ui.use_time_fixed_effects_or_dr: Use time fixed effects or Driscoll-Kraay standard errors if common shocks are plausible.
translations.analysis.ui.no_cross_sectional_dependenc: No cross-sectional dependence adjustment is suggested by this test.
translations.analysis.ui.add_time_fixed_effects_and_c: Add time fixed effects and consider Driscoll-Kraay standard errors for panel regression.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_anova_rank: Uses large-sample chi-square approximation for rank-based omnibus tests.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_anova_f: Uses Cohen's f with noncentral F approximation; repeated-measures options adjust by average correlation and epsilon.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_manova: Uses an approximate MANOVA power calculation by transforming Pillai's trace V to f2 = V / (1 - V), then applying an F-style noncentrality approximation.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_rank_ancova: Uses an ANCOVA noncentral F approximation after rank transformation, with covariate R-squared residual-variance adjustment and asymptotic relative efficiency penalty.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_ancova: Uses an ANCOVA noncentral F approximation with effect size f adjusted by the covariate-explained residual variance: f_adjusted = f / sqrt(1 - R2).
translations.sample_size.result.planning_logistic: Uses a Hsieh-style Wald approximation for a logistic regression odds ratio with event probability, predictor prevalence, and covariate R-squared adjustment.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_regression_f: Uses Cohen's f2 with a noncentral F test for overall, incremental, or interaction-term regression effects.
translations.analysis.ui.use_research_design_and_esti: Use research design and estimand to choose among GEE, LMM / GLMM, and panel models.
translations.analysis.ui.prefer_fixed_effects_when_un: Prefer fixed effects when unit-specific unobserved factors may correlate with predictors.
translations.analysis.ui.prefer_fixed_effects_when_th: Prefer fixed effects when the random-effects independence assumption is doubtful.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_mediation_fr: Uses Fritz & MacKinnon (2007) empirical Table 3 sample-size estimates for .80 power to detect the mediated effect.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_mediation_mc: Uses a Monte Carlo percentile confidence interval simulation for the indirect effect.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_mediation_bo: Uses bootstrap confidence interval simulation for the indirect effect.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_mediation_so: Uses a Sobel / first-order delta approximation for the indirect effect.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_mediation_fa: Uses Sobel, Monte Carlo percentile confidence interval, bootstrap confidence interval simulation, or Fritz & MacKinnon empirical table estimates for the indirect effect.
translations.longitudinal.mixed_message.intercept: Subject-level random intercepts are grouped by %s.
translations.longitudinal.mixed_message.slope: Subject-level random intercepts are grouped by %s, with a random slope for %s.
translations.longitudinal.mixed_message.cluster: An additional cluster-level random intercept is grouped by %s.
translations.analysis.ui.add_a_random_slope_only_when: Add a random slope only when subject-specific time trends are substantively expected and supported by the data.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_gee: Uses an independent two-group test as a baseline and multiplies by a repeated-measures design effect from the working correlation. For unstructured correlation, enter upper-triangle pairwise correlations, for example r12, r13, r23 for three time points.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_lmm_gls: Uses simulation-based power from user-specified time-specific means, residual SD, and repeated-measures correlation; nlme::gls tests the time or group x time hypothesis across simulated datasets. For unstructured correlation, enter upper-triangle pairwise correlations, for example r12, r13, r23 for three time points.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_lmm_longpowe: Uses longpower::diggle.linear.power for closed-form longitudinal linear model slope/change power with exchangeable random-intercept correlation. The standardized fixed effect is treated as the group x time slope/change difference per residual SD.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_lmm_lme: Uses simulation-based power: repeated-measures data are generated from the specified fixed effect, time points, ICC, and random-intercept LMM, then nlme::lme p-values are counted across simulations.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_survival: Uses the Schoenfeld event-based approximation: required events are determined from log hazard ratio, alpha, power, and allocation fraction, then converted to total sample size by the expected overall event probability.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_tost_exact: Uses TOSTER::power_t_TOST for exact t-based two-sample TOST equivalence power on a mean difference.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_equivalence_: Uses normal-approximation sample size for one-sided non-inferiority or TOST equivalence tests on a mean or proportion difference.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_auc: Uses the Hanley-McNeil AUC variance approximation to test one ROC AUC against a null AUC.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_diagnostic_p: Uses Buderer's precision-based formula for sensitivity or specificity, incorporating disease prevalence and desired confidence interval half-width.
translations.analysis.ui.the_reml_gradient_and_positi: The REML gradient and positive curvature checks passed.
translations.analysis.ui.review_residual_plots_and_th: Review residual plots and the scientific suitability of the selected repeated covariance.
translations.analysis.ui.residual_covariance_un_no_ra: Residual covariance: UN ; no random effects fitted.
translations.analysis.ui.residual_covariance_ar1_no_r: Residual covariance: AR1 ; no random effects fitted.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_precision_r: Uses Fisher's z transformation to approximate the sample size needed for a desired correlation confidence interval half-width.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_precision_p: Uses the normal-approximation formula n = z^2 p(1-p) / d^2 for a desired proportion confidence interval half-width.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_precision_me: Uses the normal-approximation formula n = (z SD / d)^2 for a desired mean confidence interval half-width.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_mcnemar: Uses a normal approximation to McNemar's paired binary test based on the two discordant pair probabilities p01 and p10.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_rates_nb: Uses a Wald approximation for two negative binomial rates with variance inflated by dispersion: Var(Y) = mu + dispersion * mu^2.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_rates_single: Uses the normal approximation to a Poisson rate confidence interval to estimate required person-time for a desired half-width.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_rates_poisso: Uses a Wald normal approximation for comparing two independent Poisson incidence rates with a person-time allocation ratio.
translations.analysis.ui.rows_retained_by_selected_mi: Rows retained by selected missing-data method
translations.analysis.ui.rows_excluded_by_selected_mi: Rows excluded by selected missing-data method
translations.analysis.ui.subjects_clusters_with_any_i: Subjects / clusters with any incomplete selected row
translations.analysis.ui.rows_with_any_missing_model_: Rows with any missing model term
translations.analysis.ui.rows_with_missing_id_or_time: Rows with missing ID or time
translations.analysis.ui.rows_with_missing_higher_lev: Rows with missing higher-level cluster ID
translations.sample_size.result.planning_cluster_step: Uses simulation-based power for a cross-sectional stepped-wedge cluster trial fitted with fixed period effects and a random cluster intercept.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_cluster_webp: Uses WebPower::wp.crt2arm for a parallel 2-arm continuous cluster randomized trial. The returned total cluster count is rounded up to balanced clusters per group.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_cluster_de: Uses the standard design effect DE = 1 + (m - 1) ICC to inflate an individually randomized two-group sample size, then rounds to whole clusters.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_reliability_: Uses an approximate confidence interval precision formula for Bland-Altman limits of agreement based on the SD of paired differences.
Uses an approximate normal method for Cronbach's alpha precision based on the log(1 - alpha) transformation.
Uses an approximate Fisher z precision method for intraclass correlation reliability.
Uses a large-sample normal approximation for Cohen's kappa precision assuming equal category prevalence.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_sem_complexi: Uses a model-complexity planning estimate: cases-per-free-parameter, observed/latent variable and structural path burden, and approximate detectability of expected standardized loading/path coefficients. The recommended N is the maximum of the component rules.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_sem_paramete: Uses approximate draws from a standardized SEM/CFA parameter estimate distribution. The standard error is based on a Fisher-z-style large-sample approximation with a model-complexity effective sample size adjustment; this is not full model data generation and refitting.
translations.sample_size.result.planning_sem_rmsea: Uses RMSEA-based SEM/CFA model-level power with noncentrality parameter lambda = (N - 1) df RMSEA^2 and the noncentral chi-square distribution.
translations.analysis.ui.report_why_this_longitudinal: Report why this longitudinal model matches the estimand and data structure.
translations.sample_size.result.note_mediation_sobel: Approximate mediation power using standardized a and b paths with a Sobel z approximation.
translations.sample_size.result.note_mediation_mc: Approximate mediation power using Monte Carlo percentile confidence intervals for the indirect effect.
translations.sample_size.result.note_bootstrap_counts: Bootstrap indirect effect CI simulation (%s simulations x %s bootstrap samples). This is slow and approximate.
translations.sample_size.result.note_lmm_counts: Simulation-based LMM power using nlme::lme with random intercepts (%s simulations). Results depend on variance assumptions, ICC, time points, and model structure.
translations.sample_size.result.note_gls_structure_co: GLIMMPSE-style mean/covariance simulation using nlme::gls with %s repeated-measures correlation (%s simulations).
translations.sample_size.result.note_sem_parameter_co: Approximate power simulation for a %s of %s using a large-sample standard-error approximation, a %s complexity adjustment, and %s draws per evaluated sample size. This is not a full SEM data-generation and model-refitting Monte Carlo study.
translations.analysis.ui.confirm_that_the_selected_fa: Confirm that the selected family matches the outcome scale; for count outcomes, review the Poisson dispersion-threshold screening and treat AIC/BIC as supplementary diagnostics.
translations.analysis.ui.exponentiated_coefficients_a: Exponentiated coefficients are reported as OR for binomial models, rate ratios for count models, and mean ratios for Gamma log-link models.
translations.analysis.ui.the_fitted_generalized_linea: The fitted Generalized linear mixed model (gaussian) uses Gaussian / identity.
The fitted Generalized linear mixed model (binomial) uses Binomial / logit.
The fitted Generalized linear mixed model (count) uses Count: Poisson or negative binomial / log.
The fitted Generalized linear mixed model (poisson) uses Poisson / log.
The fitted Generalized linear mixed model (negative_binomial) uses Negative binomial / log.
The fitted Generalized linear mixed model (gamma) uses Gamma / log.
translations.sample_size.result.note_t_independent: For an independent two-sample t-test, Cohen's d = t * sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2). Hedges' g applies the small-sample correction.
translations.sample_size.result.note_t_equal: For equal-sized independent groups, Cohen's d = 2t / sqrt(df + 2). Use the group-n option when n1 and n2 differ.
translations.sample_size.result.note_t_one: For a one-sample t-test, Cohen's d = t / sqrt(n).
translations.sample_size.result.note_t_paired: For a paired t-test, Cohen's dz = t / sqrt(number of pairs).
translations.sample_size.result.note_t_r: For a two-group contrast, Cohen's d can be converted from point-biserial r as d = 2r / sqrt(1 - r^2).
translations.sample_size.result.note_t_pooled: Cohen's d uses the pooled SD; Hedges' g applies the small-sample correction J = 1 - 3 / (4df - 1).
translations.analysis.ui.experimental_spss_compatibil: Experimental SPSS compatibility mode: custom GEE estimator, not the geepack estimator. This mode is not the default analysis.
translations.analysis.ui.unstructured_gee_with_parame: Unstructured GEE with parameter-count correlation correction (SPSS ADJUSTCORR=YES), Pearson scale divided by N-p, and robust sandwich standard errors. Observation weights are not supported in this mode.
translations.sample_size.result.note_proportion_trans: Proportion effect sizes are calculated from two proportions; Cohen's h uses the arcsine-square-root transformation.
translations.sample_size.result.note_w_categories: Cohen's w is calculated from observed and expected category proportions.
translations.sample_size.result.note_phi: Phi = sqrt(chi-square / N); for a 2x2 table, phi equals Cohen's w.
translations.sample_size.result.note_w_planning: Cohen's w = sqrt(chi-square / N) for goodness-of-fit or contingency chi-square effect-size planning.
translations.sample_size.result.note_point_biserial: For a two-group contrast, point-biserial r can be converted to Cohen's d as d = 2r / sqrt(1 - r^2).
translations.sample_size.result.note_pearson: Pearson r is reported directly; Fisher's z = atanh(r).
translations.sample_size.result.note_cohens_q: Cohen's q is the difference between two Fisher-z transformed correlations.
translations.sample_size.result.note_r_squared: For a single predictor, r = sqrt(R-squared); the sign is not identifiable from R-squared alone.
translations.sample_size.result.note_r_f: For a one-degree-of-freedom effect, r = sqrt(F / [F + df_error]).
translations.analysis.ui.the_fitted_gee_gaussian_uses: The fitted GEE (gaussian) uses Gaussian / identity.
translations.analysis.ui.the_fitted_gee_binomial_uses: The fitted GEE (binomial) uses Binomial / logit.
translations.analysis.ui.the_fitted_gee_count_uses_co: The fitted GEE (count) uses Count: Poisson or negative binomial / log.
translations.analysis.ui.the_fitted_gee_poisson_uses_: The fitted GEE (poisson) uses Poisson / log.
translations.analysis.ui.the_fitted_gee_gamma_uses_ga: The fitted GEE (gamma) uses Gamma / log.
translations.analysis.ui.the_fitted_marginal_negative: The fitted Marginal negative binomial GLM (subject-cluster robust SE) uses Negative binomial / log.
translations.sample_size.result.note_omega_f: Partial omega squared is approximated from F, number of groups, and total sample size.
translations.sample_size.result.note_anova_df: For one-way ANOVA, df_effect = groups - 1 and df_error = total N - groups; partial eta squared = F * df_effect / (F * df_effect + df_error).
translations.sample_size.result.note_pillai: For MANOVA planning, Pillai's trace is transformed to f2 = V / (1 - V).
translations.sample_size.result.note_wilks: Wilks' lambda is transformed with s = min(number of dependent variables, groups - 1): eta2 = 1 - lambda^(1/s), f2 = eta2 / (1 - eta2).
translations.sample_size.result.note_ancova_df: For one-way ANCOVA/group contrast planning, df_effect = groups - 1 and df_error = total N - groups; partial eta squared = F * df_effect / (F * df_effect + df_error).
translations.sample_size.result.note_logistic_d: Approximate Cohen's d = log(OR) * sqrt(3) / pi under the logistic latent-variable scale.
translations.sample_size.result.note_moderation_f2: For a single interaction increment, f2 = delta R-squared / (1 - delta R-squared).
translations.sample_size.result.note_rank_orientation: Rank-biserial correlation = 2U / (n1 n2) - 1; this is equivalent to Cliff's delta orientation.
translations.sample_size.result.note_epsilon_bound: Kruskal-Wallis epsilon squared = (H - k + 1) / (N - k), bounded at 0.
translations.sample_size.result.note_matched_correcti: Matched-pair odds ratio = b / c for discordant pairs; a 0.5 continuity correction is used if either discordant cell is zero.
translations.sample_size.result.note_matched_probabil: Matched-pair odds ratio = p01 / p10 using the two discordant probabilities.
translations.sample_size.result.note_gee_supplied: Uses the supplied standardized mean difference d.
translations.sample_size.result.note_glmm_logit: For a binary logit GLMM, the model-scale fixed effect is log(OR). Approximate latent-scale d = log(OR) * sqrt(3) / pi.
translations.sample_size.result.note_glmm_probs: For binary outcomes, probabilities are converted to odds ratio; Cohen's h is also reported for the marginal proportion contrast.
translations.sample_size.result.note_glmm_log: For a Poisson or negative-binomial GLMM with log link, the model-scale fixed effect is log(IRR), and IRR = exp(B).
translations.sample_size.result.note_glmm_rates: For count outcomes with a log link, the marginal rate ratio is equivalent to IRR when offsets/exposure are handled consistently.
translations.sample_size.result.note_glmm_identity: For a Gaussian identity-link mixed model, standardized effect d = fixed-effect coefficient B / residual SD.
translations.sample_size.result.note_lmm_vectors: GLIMMPSE-style effect uses the last-minus-first mean contrast divided by residual SD, with repeated-measures planning adjustment.
translations.sample_size.result.note_lmm_spss_omnibus: For the LMM fixed-effect omnibus test, partial eta squared is approximated from the SPSS F test as F * df_effect / (F * df_effect + df_error).
translations.sample_size.result.note_lmm_spss_pairwis: Pairwise Cohen's dz is calculated as mean difference / sqrt(Var_i + Var_j - 2Cov_ij), using the LMM covariance estimates.
translations.sample_size.result.note_lmm_spss_combine: For the LMM fixed-effect omnibus test, partial eta squared is approximated from the SPSS F test as F * df_effect / (F * df_effect + df_error). Pairwise Cohen's dz is calculated as mean difference / sqrt(Var_i + Var_j - 2Cov_ij), using the LMM covariance estimates.
translations.sample_size.result.note_equivalence_insi: Equivalence distance = margin - abs(observed effect); positive values are inside the equivalence margin.
translations.sample_size.result.note_noninferiority_a: Non-inferiority distance = margin + observed effect when the non-inferiority boundary is -margin; positive values are above the boundary.
translations.sample_size.result.note_cluster_binary: Binary cluster effect uses Cohen's h; planning effect = h / sqrt(1 + (m - 1)ICC).
translations.sample_size.result.note_cluster_stepped: Stepped-wedge planning effect applies a simple cluster design effect multiplied by periods / (periods - 1).
translations.analysis.ui.draw_paths_on_the_shared_can: Draw paths on the shared canvas. The design variables set under Complex Samples are applied automatically.
translations.sample_size.result.note_agreement_approx: Bland-Altman limits of agreement are approximately mean difference +/- 1.96 * SD of paired differences.
translations.sample_size.result.note_sem_parameter: Standardized SEM parameter effect is the expected standardized coefficient; Fisher's z is atanh(parameter).
translations.sample_size.result.note_sem_rmsea: RMSEA effect is the difference between alternative and null RMSEA; noncentrality difference per N is df * (RMSEA_alt^2 - RMSEA_null^2).
translations.sample_size.result.note_plan_t_two: Exact independent two-sample t-test power calculation using Cohen's d.
translations.sample_size.result.note_plan_t_paired: Exact paired t-test power calculation using dz, the standardized mean of paired differences.
translations.sample_size.result.note_plan_t_one: Exact one-sample t-test power calculation using standardized mean difference.
translations.sample_size.result.note_plan_t_unequal_n: Normal approximation for unequal-allocation independent means using Cohen's d.
translations.sample_size.result.note_plan_t_unequal_p: Approximate power for unequal-allocation independent means based on the normal distribution.
translations.sample_size.result.note_plan_rank_are: Approximate nonparametric sample size using ARE = 0.955 relative to the corresponding t-test under normal data.
translations.analysis.ui.categorical_reference_levels: Categorical reference levels and contrast coding
translations.sample_size.result.note_power_t_two: Exact independent two-sample t-test power calculation.
translations.sample_size.result.note_power_rank: Approximate nonparametric power using ARE = 0.955 relative to the corresponding t-test under normal data.
translations.sample_size.result.note_prop_two_n: Normal approximation for two independent proportions.
translations.sample_size.result.note_prop_two_power: Approximate power for two independent proportions.
translations.sample_size.result.note_prop_one_n: Approximation for one proportion against null p = 0.50.
translations.sample_size.result.note_prop_one_power: Approximate power for one proportion against null p = 0.50.
translations.sample_size.result.note_correlation_z: Fisher z approximation for Pearson correlation.
translations.sample_size.result.note_chisquare_ncp: Chi-square test using Cohen's w and noncentral chi-square distribution.
translations.analysis.ui.emphasize_uncertainty_in_str: Emphasize uncertainty in stratum curves and comparison tests.
translations.sample_size.result.note_plan_kw: Approximate Kruskal-Wallis sample size using Cohen's f and noncentral chi-square distribution.
translations.sample_size.result.note_plan_friedman: Approximate Friedman test using Kendall's W and noncentral chi-square distribution.
